# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

The code shows a mostly healthy Next.js site, with two quick fixes and a few smaller ones. Nothing was left unknown. Both numbers are read from code, not measured on a live site. I assumed you want AI search tools to find the site, which matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`. I sampled 4 indexable routes (`/`, `/pricing`, `/docs`, `/blog`). `/thank-you` is deliberately noindex and isn't in the sitemap or menu, so I left it out.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Tell crawlers where your sitemap is
- **Why it matters:** `robots.txt` is the first file crawlers read. Without a `Sitemap:` line they have no pointer to your list of pages, even though `sitemap.xml` exists.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:5`
- **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` is the last line, and the file has no `Sitemap:` line at all.
- **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 = 80.

### 2. Declare the page language
- **Why it matters:** the `lang` attribute tells machines and screen readers what language the site is in. It's missing on every page, and `geo.config.json` already says `en`.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small. Change it to `<html lang="en">`.
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 = 80. Doing items 1 and 2 together gives 20.5 ÷ 23 = 89.

### 3. Add a canonical to Docs and Blog
- **Why it matters:** a canonical says which address is the main one for a page. Only Home and Pricing declare one.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` and `app/blog/page.tsx` (it has no metadata at all)
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };`
- **Size:** Small. Add `alternates: { canonical: 'https://www.ledger.example/docs' }`, and the same for `/blog`. `/blog` needs a server `metadata` export, so it must move out of the `'use client'` file. Item 4 below does that.
- **Score after this:** 17.5 ÷ 23 = 76.

## All results

| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. The page is in the sitemap and the menu. 3 of 4 routes are clear. |

## Other problems found

- **Pricing is noindexed but promoted, and its canonical points at itself:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`: `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. It appears in `public/sitemap.xml:4` and the menu at `app/layout.tsx:13`. If you want Pricing found, remove the `robots` entry. If you don't, remove it from the sitemap.
- **Blog loads from `/api/posts`, but no such route exists in the repo:** `app/blog/page.tsx:8`: `fetch('/api/posts')`. If it's served elsewhere, ignore this. Otherwise the page will render empty.

## Worth considering

- **Pricing promises more than it shows:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Plans for every team size.'`, while the page says only `Free for up to three people.` A short list of the plans and their prices, as text, would match the promise.
- **Docs is a single sentence:** `app/docs/page.tsx:3`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` Visitors asking how to set up Ledger get no steps. Written setup steps would give machines something to quote.
- **Blog posts have no pages of their own:** `app/blog/page.tsx:10`: `<article key={p.id}>{p.title}</article>`. Each post could get its own address and be listed in the sitemap.
- **Home page says little about the business:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Invoices, expenses and reports in one place.` Organization or SoftwareApplication JSON-LD could label what Ledger is, but only once real details (name, logo, and so on) are in the page.
- **Head basics:** `app/layout.tsx:3` sets only the title, description and `metadataBase`. Next.js adds `charset` and `viewport` by default, so that's fine. Social-share tags (`openGraph`) are absent. They would only help if people share your pages.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. If you have access logs, `geopilot logs <access log>` checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live-only checks:** real status codes, redirects and `X-Robots-Tag` headers (GEO-014), whether sitemap URLs answer 200 (GEO-011), and the rendered text ratio on `/blog` (GEO-003).

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, which matches your config.
- The blank `Sitemap:` line and the Pricing noindex are mistakes, not choices. If Pricing is meant to stay hidden, the score changes only by removing it from the sitemap and menu.
- No framework config, middleware or hosting setup outside the repo changes headers or robots rules.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
